analysis:
Examined all six batch analyses and independently checked the three replayed patches. provider-ci-build/action.yml:64,91,146,154,160,181 gates its cache operations on CI_ACTIONS_CACHE without removing existing trusted-save requirements. provider-release-build/action.yml:120,165,185,263,275,392 applies the same gate while leaving fixture preparation and build/test execution intact. This resolves the analyses' nested-composite propagation question for these supplied changes.
ci-master.yml:80–89 and 230–239 sets the flag before cache restores; restores/saves at 102,143,249,290 honor it. Its new validation at 111–136 and 258–283 rejects links, active hooks and selected executable/include configuration before existing Git integrity checks and checkout. This is hardening, not evidence of a new cache-poisoning regression. Validation does not authenticate cache contents; suppressed parser/traversal failures cannot justify claiming arbitrary cached Git state is safe.
Build-source and artifact integrity implicate A-011/A-017 and T-013/T-034/T-054; cold builds also affect availability. No supported regression in those contracts was identified. No supplied change alters serving authorization, attestation, billing, privileged helpers or hop-by-hop inference encryption. Actions build caches are distinct from the consumer KV cache in T-041.
Remaining material uncertainty: RUNNER_NAME and DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL presence only select whether caching runs; actual cache redirection, authentication and branch/PR isolation remain runner-side contracts not established here. Integration replay omits 39 of 42 reviewed source units, so the desktop, landing, release-cache and later provider-tests changes, documentation assertions and complete scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py changes cannot be independently validated from the prior analyses alone. Further review should confirm those callers gate every cache operation and that provisioning supplies the claimed dedicated endpoint. Missing evidence is not a finding or a safety conclusion.
